podcast.body: Oasis announced the release of this single for August 14, 1995, which directly led to the "Battle of Britpop" when Blur chose the same release date for their single "Country House." The single ultimately lost the chart battle to Blur. "Oasis announced that role with it would be released on August 14th, 1995."

podcast.body: Originally slated for mid-September 1995, Oasis deliberately moved its release date to mid-August, and then to August 14, 1995, to clash directly with Blur's "Country House." Despite selling 216,000 copies, it was outsold by Blur's single in the "epic Britpop showdown." "It was called Roll With It."

podcast.body: Released on August 14, 1995, this single was at the center of a highly publicized "record war" with Blur's "Country House." The intense competition captivated Britain, with the two singles collectively accounting for almost 30% of all UK singles sold that week. Despite the hype, Oasis's "Roll With It" sold 220,000 copies in its first week, falling short of Blur's 270,000 copies. "In one corner, it was Oasis and rolled with it."

podcast.body: This single was at the center of the highly publicized "Great Battle of Britpop," released simultaneously with Blur's "Country House" in 1995. Oasis, then a younger band under considerable pressure from a multinational label, strongly engaged in this rivalry. "el lanzamiento simultáneo, The Roll with it, The Oasis, con Country House de Blur el mismo día."

This single, released in August 1995 from the album *Morning Glory*, was considered relatively weak compared to Blur's "Country House" single. It was easily outsold by Blur during the "Great Battle of Britpop," despite the overall strength of Oasis's album. "Oasis salía con uno de los singles relativamente flojos del disco. De manera que fue fácil para Blurba tiremventas el lanzamiento del single de Oasis"
